acceptanceCriteria: A discrimination witness whose `mutants` exceeds `bounds.maxMutants`, or whose survivors are inconsistent with `survived`, fails `invalid-field` in the native reader and the portable consumer.
protocol/cem-0.3 gains refusal cases for both inputs and native and portable still agree on every packet case.
The 0.3 spec names the rule next to the existing count rule.
body: Source: decision 0523 (docs/decisions/0523-cem-1-0-rc3-verifier-computed-support-2026-10-11.md) and build-log docs/build-log/2026-10-11-cem-1-0-expert-panel.md, origin/main fb11b2274. Repro: a cem/0.3 map hunk with `discriminates: {mutants:1000000, killed:1000000, survived:0, survivors:[], bounds:{maxHunks:1,maxMutants:1,wallTimeSeconds:1}, state:"discriminates"}` on a one-line hunk. Expected: `invalid-field`. Actual: accepted; `discriminationCounts` in internal/cem/wire/discriminate.go checks only killed+survived<=mutants and `validateDiscriminationBounds` validates the bounds alone. Proposed CEM-V1-070. Version: 1.0.0-rc.3 build 407.
title: cem 0.3: discrimination witness counts are never compared with `bounds.maxMutants`, so `mutants: 1000000` under `maxMutants: 1` is accepted
